title.quote: C LOSING THE G AP BETWEEN TD L EARNING AND S UPERVISED L EARNING – A G ENERALISATION P OINT OF V IEW
title.value: Closing the Gap between TD Learning and Supervised Learning – A Generalisation Point of View

extractions.description: The paper formalises the RL "stitching" property as a form of combinatorial generalisation, argues that supervised-learning-based RL (outcome-conditioned behavioural cloning) methods lack it, constructs new offline maze datasets that explicitly test for it, and proposes a temporal data augmentation that improves stitching for OCBC methods (RvS, DT) on state-based and image-based goal- and return-conditioned tasks.

type.quote: On 10 different environments, including both state and image based tasks, and goal and return conditioning, adding data augmentation improves the generalisation capabilities of SL approaches by up to a factor of 2.5.
type.justification: The paper combines theory with extensive empirical evaluation across 10 environments and ablations; experiments dominate.

name.quote: Some reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms can stitch pieces of experience to solve a task never seen before during training.
name.justification: The paper studies RL algorithms and their stitching property.

name.quote: Our work focuses on the offline RL setting where the agent has access to a fixed dataset of N trajectories
name.justification: The work focuses on the offline RL setting and contributes new offline datasets.

name.quote: Conditional imitation learning methods do not have the combinatorial generalisation property.
name.justification: Outcome conditional behavioral cloning is a conditional imitation learning setting.
